Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The dashboards looked great — the product team is sold on the visualization layer, but our finance team is concerned about how observability costs will scale. They specifically asked for:

- A clear line-item split between trace retention (ingest + storage) and the advanced dashboard seat/license cost
- An example bill for a 6-month pilot with: 10M trace events/day, retention options at 30/90/365 days, and 8 dashboard seats
- Any available pilot credits or temporary discounts so we can validate business value without a big upfront commitment

Can you provide a short sample invoice and confirm whether trace storage can be metered independently from dashboard feature bundles? Also, if there are options to cap retention spend (e.g., roll-off policies or archival credits), that would help our procurement team approve a PoC.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — can we aim for an answer by next Tuesday?

Best,

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and for the product feedback.

Short answer: yes, we can present an itemized pricing view and meter trace retention separately from dashboard seats/features. Below is what I can do for you by next Tuesday:

1) A sample 6-month invoice with three retention tiers (30/90/365 days) modeled on your 10M events/day assumption. The model will show ingest, storage, and query costs, plus dashboard licensing.
2) A recommended pilot structure: 8 dashboard seats, retention set to 90 days by default with automatic archive to cheaper blob storage after 90 days (optional).
3) A proposal for pilot credits: we can offer a $15k observability credit that covers storage + dashboard seats for up to 6 weeks of usage during the PoC, subject to a signed pilot SOW.
4) Spend control options: per-tenant retention caps, egress caps, and low-cost archival with lifecycle rules — all configurable at rollout.

I attached a preliminary SKU sheet (RDW_Observability_SKU_Pricing_0428.pdf) and will have the sample invoice and a one-page decision map ready by 2028-05-01.

Quick clarification for procurement: our advanced dashboards are licensed per-seat with an 'enterprise features' add-on (alerts, multi-workspace joins); we can separate that charge from trace storage in the contract so you can attribute costs to different internal owners.

Kimberly — can you confirm whether we can extend the pilot credit to include an extra 2 weeks of data (so Elena's team can run two overlapping sprints)? Jordan — please flag any quota or retention-cap automation that would require changes to the SOW.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni

Vivek / Elena —

We can extend the pilot credit by 2 weeks (so total 8 weeks) provided DataVista agrees to a short evaluation SOW and shares a lightweight usage telemetry file at the end of the pilot for us to assess savings. Key points:

- Pilot credit: $15k + 2-week extension (total $15k) — covers ingest, storage up to the modeled 10M events/day, and 8 dashboard seats. If usage exceeds baseline by >30%, we'll discuss top-up credits.
- Metering: trace ingest/storage will be billed on usage under the 'trace.storage' SKU. Dashboard seats and the advanced-features add-on will be separate SKUs—listed line items in the invoice.
- Billing controls: we can enable a hard retention cap and automated archival to blob storage after N days. We can also set a monthly spend alarm in the console and set an auto-throttle policy if spend exceeds threshold.

Action items for DataVista (small asks to speed approval):
- Sign the pilot SOW (I can drop a minimal one-page SOW into DocuSign)
- Confirm whether you want archival at 90 or 365 days for the pilot
- Share the internal billing owner (email) so we can cc them on the sample invoice

Elena — I'll prepare the sample invoice now and include both a metered scenario and a slab scenario (50% discount slabs at 6-month commit) so your finance team can compare.
